Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Some people seem to be unaware of the 'job description' of the rules
team, so allow me a moment to clarify:

The Rules Team makes rules.

The current RT has approached this task from a balance-and-correctness
perspective. Meaning that balance is paramount, and correctness follows
closely behing. So errata are issued to preserve balance, even if they
change a card or a rule into something that it was not designed to be.

If balance is not compromised, then rulings/errata are issued to
maintain the design (original intent) of the cards and rules, in so far
as the intent is known or can be reasonably assumed.

While votes and diatribes and other assorted "this sucks, change it"
rants have some utility (in illuminating areas for the RT to examine
more closely), unless they show how balance has been compromised or
how correctness has been sacrificed when balance was not at risk,
they will likely not bring about any change in the official rulings.

The best path to take to get a new ruling issued or an old ruling
overturned is to show how the new ruling (old lack of an existing
ruling) would fix some problem with the game.

--
To address one other point: the RT has nothing to do with DCI
Sanctioning. The only official interface between the RT and the DCI
is in the area of the banned/restricted list. The RT can make
recommendations for such lists. That is all.

--
L. Scott Johnson (vte...@wizards.com) VTES Net.Rep for Wizards of the Coast.

Messages.Author: mboh...@shout.net
Messages.Body:
In article <6qp1df$gfr$1...@nnrp1.dejanews.com>,
CPilh...@bhak12.ac.at wrote:

[ Wake errata ]

> But the actual ruling makes Forced Awakening a better choice (even
> with the cost)! I still don't see that WwEF is unbalanced.

Actually, Forced Awakening is not always a better choice. What if you
are using bleed bounce as bleed defense? If you are using Forced Awakening,
you are paying 2 blood for each deflection. Against a heavy bleeder, your
vampires will be empty pretty quickly. If you use Wake, you don't spend
the extra blood, and you have to wait until your turn to redraw.

> But, if you still insist that it is, why is "don't replace until the end
> of the current turn" not enough? I really can't see it.

From what I recall, one of the big problems with Wake is that you can play
it during anyone's turn even though you have no chance of blocking one of
their actions. So let's say you have 3 Wakes in your hand, but none of
the cards you need. With your suggested errata, you could still dump all
three if you wanted with no adverse side effect.

In my decks, I've been doing the following. In intercept decks and combat
decks I use Forced Awakening because I really want to block. So if
I don't block, I lose a blood. In decks that use weenies, need lots of
blood for other things (like Ravnos and Lasombra), or use bleed bounce,
I use Wake.

Mike

Under 7/7 you can dump as many Wakes as you want as well. There's almost
no difference. With 7/7 you just wait until you predator takes his last
action, dump all Wakes, and then during your untap get a full hand again.

Btw, who would dump Wakes???? They are (at least in my environment) a
really important defense. If you pack so many Wakes in your deck that you
have to dump them, something with your deck is not right. Too many Wakes
take important deck space!!! That's a cost, too.

Well, to this date I haven't seen a single player dumping wakes en masse.
O.K., I know of situations, where you have a Wake, but you have no
intercept, bleed bounce, reduce bleed in your hand; so you play the
wake, hoping to draw a usable card for the *next* action. That's it.
But playing 4 or 5 Wakes in a row, well that has never been observed in
our play-environment.

-Carl, VEKN Prince of Vienna

Now, I'm playing Devil's advocate a bit, since I don't think Wake was
broken, although it wasn't in the spirit of the rest of the game.

(which are inherently weak), and so hardly broken I'll agree.
